prompt.context: Your client is a large retail bank in the U.S. looking to move its current outsourced call center from India to Africa. The client is currently evaluating 3 possible countries as a target location. The call center handles two types of calls: Customer Service Calls (e.g., account locked, password reset) and Sales Calls (pushing new services to new and existing clients, e.g., credit cards). This is the bank's first time operating in Africa.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate each of these three potential African sites for the bank's call center relocation?

clarifying_info.q: What is the primary driver of this move?
clarifying_info.a: Cost reduction — the client wants to lower the cost of running the call center.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current annual cost of the call center?
What is the investment required to set up the call center in any of the three countries?
How many employees does the current call center have?
What is the average call duration?
How many working hours per day and working days per year?
clarifying_info.a: 8 hours per day; assume 300 days per year.

clarifying_info.q: Is security cost included in the numbers?

exhibits.title: Typical Cost Structure for Call Center
exhibits.shows: A bar/stacked chart showing the breakdown of a typical call center's cost structure as percentages of total cost.

exhibits.title: Call Demand Data by Country
exhibits.shows: A table comparing the current call center with three candidate African countries across key operational metrics.

data.Note: Current call center has 400 employees. Assume 300 days/yr for annual labor cost.

framework: Financial analysis: Compare operating costs (labor, rent, utilities, overhead) and investment cost between current India setup and each African country; isolate the incremental savings
Labor as key driver: Recognize that labor is ~40% of cost structure and the primary source of savings; all other costs (rent, utilities, misc.) are assumed equal across locations
Investment and payback: Evaluate whether the $36M upfront investment can be recovered in a reasonable time given annual savings
Firm considerations: Alignment with strategy, lack of prior Africa experience, opportunity cost of capital, risk to service quality for customers
Market (Africa) considerations: Availability of English-speaking labor with banking knowledge, political stability, availability of infrastructure (internet, electricity), competitor precedent

questions.prompt: Question 1: What elements would you consider when evaluating the 3 countries?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will structure their evaluation across Financial and Non-Financial dimensions. Financial: operating costs (labor, rent, utilities, transport, overhead) with focus on changes from current state; investment cost and recoverability. Non-Financial — Firm: strategic alignment, Africa experience, opportunity cost, customer service quality risk. Non-Financial — Market: availability of English-speaking labor with banking knowledge, political stability, infrastructure availability, whether competitors have already done this.

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are typical costs of running a call center, and which would be lower in Africa?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify labor as the main savings lever (40% of cost per Exhibit 1; all other cost lines are assumed unchanged). Then push candidate to quantify: using 36,000 total calls/day as the demand constraint, determine how many employees each country needs at its utilization rate, compute annual labor cost, and compare to current $24M labor cost (=$60M x 40%). Country B yields the greatest savings at $12.48M/yr, making it the top choice. Strong candidates note upfront that Countries A and B have the same utilization but B has a lower rate, so B is strictly better than A. Utilization is expected to improve over time for new centers but candidates should ignore this in calculations.

math.setup: Total calls/day = 400 employees x (75% utilization x 8 hrs x 60 min/hr) / 4 min per call = 400 x 90 calls/employee = 36,000 calls/day. For each country, back-solve employees needed: Employees = 36,000 / (utilization x 8 hrs x 60 min / 4 min). Annual labor cost = employees x cost/employee x 300 days. Cost/employee/day = labor rate x 8 hrs.
steps: Total calls/day = 400 x (0.75 x 8 x 60 / 4) = 400 x 90 = 36,000 calls
Country A: employees = 36,000 / (0.50 x 8 x 60 / 4) = 36,000 / 60 = 600 employees; cost/employee/day = $10 x 8 = $80; annual = 600 x $80 x 300 = $14,400,000
Country B: employees = 36,000 / (0.50 x 8 x 60 / 4) = 600 employees; cost/employee/day = $8 x 8 = $64; annual = 600 x $64 x 300 = $11,520,000
Country C: employees = 36,000 / (0.25 x 8 x 60 / 4) = 1,200 employees; cost/employee/day = $6 x 8 = $48; annual = 1,200 x $48 x 300 = $17,280,000
Savings vs. current — Country A: $24M - $14.4M = $9.6M/yr; Country B: $24M - $11.52M = $12.48M/yr; Country C: $24M - $17.28M = $6.72M/yr
Country B has the highest savings ($12.48M/yr) and same utilization as A, so it is the best choice
math.answer: Country B is the optimal choice with annual labor savings of $12.48M. Country A saves $9.6M; Country C saves only $6.72M.

questions.prompt: Question 3: If the investment in each country is $36M, what is the payback period for the country you selected (Country B)?
questions.guidance: Tests basic payback period concept. Strong candidates will mention discount rate (but can ignore it in the calculation). Payback period = Investment / Annual Savings = $36M / $12.48M ≈ 2.88 years. Then ask candidate to brainstorm ways the call center could generate additional revenue to shorten payback.

math.setup: Payback Period = Investment Cost / Annual Savings

brainstorming.prompt: Are there ways the call center can generate revenue to offset costs and shorten the payback period?

categories.name: Food & Amenities
ideas: Cafeteria that sells food to employees

categories.name: Childcare & Community Services
ideas: Day care facilities for working parents

categories.name: Facility Utilization
ideas: Alternate use of facilities as a training center

categories.name: Media & Advertising
ideas: Advertising revenue from posters and signage in common areas

recommendation: The client should move its call center to Country B, as it is the most cost-effective option based on both employee labor rate ($8/hr) and productivity (same 50% utilization as Country A at a lower cost), generating $12.48M in annual savings and a ~2.9-year payback on the $36M investment
risks: Political instability in the region could disrupt operations
Service quality may deteriorate given new market inexperience and lower utilization (50% vs. current 75%)
No prior experience operating in Country B creates execution risk
Long-term labor cost inflation could erode savings over time
next_steps: Work with local governments to gain support and facilitate the investment
Consider a pilot or phased rollout to manage service quality risk before full transition
Identify additional revenue opportunities and cost savings initiatives (e.g., amenities, facility reuse) to offset any future rise in labor costs
Implement measures and incentives to improve utilization of Country B employees toward current 75% benchmark
